name: Small Craft Frames
description: Community frames published by Small Craft.

items.name: Assignments
items.description: What's due, and where you stand. Add your courses with their credit weight, then put each piece of work in with its due date and what fraction of the grade it carries. The frame opens on the work: overdue first, then this week, then later, with the nearest deadline counted in days rather than dates. Tick something off and it lifts out of the list. The other half is the arithmetic students do on the back of an envelope — each course's weighted grade so far, computed from what has actually been marked, and a GPA across courses by credit. Space editors add and tick; everyone else, including a study group the frame is shared with, sees the same board live. Courses and work live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement.

items.name: Bookmarks
items.description: A place to put links so you can find them again. Paste a URL anywhere in the frame and it saves itself — no form, no dialog — reading the site's name off the address and colouring it so the same site always looks the same. The search box is the frame's real interface: it filters by title, address and tag as you type, because a link you cannot find again is the same as one you never saved. Tag anything, filter by tag, rename what the URL got wrong. Space editors save and edit; everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, can read and follow the same links. Nothing is fetched from the sites you save: this frame asks for no network access at all, so a private bookmark stays a private bookmark. Links live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement.

items.name: Calendar
items.description: A simple shared calendar, unique per placement. Space editors add events on a given day or set them to repeat weekly (for example every Mon/Wed/Fri at 3pm) until an end date or forever, each with an optional time, length, color, link, and note; everyone else sees a clean read-only view, including anyone the space owner shares the frame publicly with. Switch between a month grid and a week view with events laid out by time of day. Timed events are authored in your own time zone and automatically shifted to each viewer's local time, so everyone sees the right moment wherever they are. Recurring events can be deleted just for one day, from a day onward, or entirely, and an event's link opens in the native browser (or a new tab on the web). The view also adapts to its size — the full month/week views when there's room, and a compact upcoming-events agenda once the tile gets small, so it stays usable down to about 200×200. The whole calendar lives in a single JSON file in a per-placement folder. No database or sync tables.

items.name: CamJam
items.description: A tiny, low-bandwidth webcam feed for a space: a stopmotion camera share rather than a video call. One member at a time shares their webcam as a small JPEG still, sent on an interval and fanned out live to everyone viewing the placement, captioned with the sharer's name and how long ago the still was taken. The stopmotion pacing is the whole idea, since a still every few seconds costs a fraction of a video call and reads as presence rather than surveillance. Cadence and detail are a single owner setting that moves them together, from a 100px thumbnail twice a second up to a 1920px still once a minute, so the choice is smoothness or sharpness rather than more or less bandwidth. Any member can start sharing, pick which camera to use, take over an active feed, or rename the frame in place. Only members are ever asked for their camera; viewers just watch. Nothing is recorded: the current still lives in memory on the host device and disappears when sharing stops. There is no microphone and no audio of any kind. Whether people outside the space can watch simply follows the frame's own share key, so there is no second visibility switch to find.

items.name: Checklist
items.description: A simple, collaborative to-do list. Each placement is its own list — any member of the space can add tasks, cycle each task through three states (unstarted, in-progress, complete), drag to reorder, and delete. Non-members get a live read-only view. Items, ordering, and states are stored in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Chore Chart
items.description: Who does what, and how it's going. Space editors add recurring chores, give each one to a person and a rhythm (daily, weekly, monthly, or just once), and tick them off as they get done. Every person gets their own card in their own colour, showing what's still open, what's already handled, and how long a streak they're on. A chore comes back by itself when its next turn arrives, so the chart is always about this week rather than a list that grows forever. Everyone else, including anyone the chart is shared with publicly, sees the same board live and read-only. Chores live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement; the owner can move them to a shared space table so other frames can work with the same rows.

items.name: Class Schedule
items.description: Your week, laid out. Put each class on the days it meets with a time and a room, and the frame draws the timetable — only the hours you actually have classes in, only the days you actually use, so a Monday-to-Friday term never wastes half the grid on an empty weekend. A line tracks the current time across today's column, and the frame says what is next and when, so the common question is answered before you read anything. Share the placement with a roommate or a study group and everybody sees the same week. Space editors set the timetable; everyone else, including anyone it is shared with publicly, can read it. Classes live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement.

items.name: Community Home
items.description: A minimal website builder for a community home page. Admins configure the title, color, sections, and links; anonymous visitors see the published public page.

items.name: Community Library
items.description: Track items shared by a community — books, tools, gear — and who has them checked out. Items and members live in shared SyncTables (the members table is compatible with Member Manager so the same roster can be reused). Per-placement preferences (org name, borrow durations, owner-only edit) are stored in a local JSON file.

items.name: Discussion Channel
items.description: A per-placement realtime chat channel. Members chat, react with Phosphor Light icons, and delete their own messages; owners can rename the channel, pick a theme, and choose whether Viewer-role members can participate. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, read the channel live without posting.

items.name: Family Budget
items.description: An envelope-lite family budget, unique per placement: money in, money out, categorized, one month at a time. Space editors record income and expenses against channel-colored category envelopes, set a monthly budget per envelope, and step through months to watch spending fill each bar. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only view of the month. Categories and transactions live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement, every change is pushed live to all viewers, and the owner can graduate a placement's data to shared tables so other frames can bind the same rows.

items.name: File Folder
items.description: A simple shared file bucket, unique per placement. Members (or just the owner — the owner chooses) can add files by clicking 'Add file' or dragging them in from the desktop. The owner sets who may add files, a max file size, and a max number of files. Anyone who can open the frame can list and download its files, so sharing the frame publicly shares the folder. Files live in the frame's own data folder in a per-placement subfolder; only the owner's sharing preferences are stored, in a single JSON file. No database or sync tables.

items.name: Flashcards
items.description: Decks you can share, with a schedule that stays yours. Cards live in the space, so a study group builds one deck together and everybody drills the same material — but what you have learned is counted per person, so your intervals never move because a classmate answered well. Reviewing uses SM-2, the spaced-repetition schedule Anki is built on: rate a card and it comes back tomorrow, in six days, or in a month, depending on how well you have been doing with it. Each answer shows what it will cost you, so choosing is a decision rather than a guess. Space editors write the cards; anyone in the space can study them. Decks, cards and each person's progress live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement.

items.name: Focus Timer
items.description: One clock, shared by everyone in the space. Turn the dial like a kitchen timer to set the length, press the middle to start, and the ring drains for everybody at once — a study room, a work sprint, a twenty-minute tidy that the whole house can see counting down. Whoever started it and what it is for are written under the dial. Space editors drive the timer; everyone else, including anyone the timer is shared with publicly, watches the same countdown live. There is no clock running on a server: the host stores the moment the session ends and every device works out the rest for itself, so the numbers agree even if a device sleeps.

items.name: ASCII Runner
items.description: A retro side-scrolling ASCII game where you jump over rocks and duck under birds. Use arrow keys to survive as long as you can!

items.name: Dice Roller
items.description: Simple dice roller. Roll via the UI or HTTP API; result is broadcast to all viewers of a frame instance.

items.name: Pancake Stacker
items.description: Simple solo arcade game. A pancake swings back and forth at the top of the griddle — tap, click, or hit space to drop it onto the stack. Each pancake trims to the overlap with the one below, so the tower narrows as you climb. Miss entirely and the stack topples. High score per placement.

items.name: Garden Gnome
items.description: An at-a-glance helper for home gardeners. Set a location, pick your soil, tick the plants you grow, and Garden Gnome fetches local weather (Open-Meteo, keyless) every 15 minutes — past 5 days plus the next 24 hours — and shows three color-coded dots on a +/- spectrum next to each plant for water, temperature, and sunlight so you know when a plant is being naturally pampered or stressed. Space editors set the garden up; everyone else, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, gets the same read-only board with the location withheld.

items.name: Garden Planner
items.description: Lay out a garden as snap-to-grid plots on a soil-toned canvas. Each plot is given a name, assigned to a person, tagged with the plant families growing in it, and stamped with when and at what stage it was planted. The frame pulls the last seven days of weather from Open-Meteo for the garden's location and tints every plot with a stress gradient — green when the plants are comfortable, red when the recent heat, rain or sun has been hard on what is planted there, worked out per plant family and softened by how much shade the bed gets. Plots start on the host device; the owner can move them to a shared space table, and can separately link an existing member roster (the schema matches Member Manager) so plots can be assigned to real people instead of typed-in names. Everyone else, including anyone the garden is shared with publicly, sees the same layout live and read-only.

items.name: Gift List
items.description: A wish list that can keep a secret. Everyone adds what they would like, and anyone else can quietly claim an item so two people don't buy the same thing — but the person the gift is for never sees the claims. They see their own list exactly as they wrote it, plus an honest note that something is being kept from them, which is the fun part. Works for a family Christmas, a birthday, or a baby shower, and the list can be shared publicly so relatives with no account can still see what is wanted and put their name on something. Wishes live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement; the owner can move them to a shared space table.

items.name: Grocery List
items.description: The realtime shared shopping list, unique per placement. Space editors add items with a quantity and an aisle category, tick things off as they land in the cart, and sweep everything bought with one clear. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees the same list live and read-only. Items live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement, and every check is pushed instantly to all viewers. The owner can move the list to a shared space table, after which the Meal Planner can send a week's ingredients straight into the same list.

items.name: Habit Tracker
items.description: One line per habit, one square per day, filled in when you did it. The grid runs right up to today and stretches as far back as the frame is wide, so a narrow tile shows the last fortnight and a wide one shows months — the same picture either way, just more of it. Tap today's square to mark it, or tap back a few days if you forgot to. Each habit keeps a current run and its best run, and the run is the point: the grid makes a gap visible in a way a checkbox never does. Space editors mark and edit; everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees the same grid live. Habits and their marks live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement.

items.name: Help Desk
items.description: Anonymous visitors submit a message with email (plus admin-configured fields); known users in the space see a realtime inbox of incoming correspondence.

items.name: Kanban Board
items.description: A drag-and-drop task board, unique per placement. Space editors organize work as cards in channel-colored columns: add, rename, recolor, and reorder columns, drag cards between them, and keep details and a short label on each card. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only view of the board. Cards and columns live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Local Device Controller
items.description: Generic control panel for a local Upline serial device: builds its interface from the device's own schema. Place it more than once to control several devices independently.

local_devices.description: read and control any connected device

items.name: Market Weather
items.description: A turnout forecaster for outdoor commerce — farmers markets, festivals, food trucks, street vendors, walkable storefronts. Set a location and Market Weather pulls 72 hours of weather from Open-Meteo (keyless), compares it against the last 30 days' local norms, and folds in temperature comfort, rain, UV, daylight, wind, weekend bonus, and time-of-day into a single composite turnout curve. The graph overlays each contributing factor as a faint band (daytime in pale yellow, rain in blue rising from the bottom, extreme heat/cold in red, weekend bonus in green) so you can see at a glance WHY the bold turnout line moves the way it does — and plan how much to stock, bake, or brew for the days ahead.

items.name: Meal Planner
items.description: A weekly meal planner, unique per placement. Space editors lay out breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks across a seven day week, step between weeks, and keep servings and notes on every meal. On its own it is a freeform planner; link a shared recipes table for a recipe picker on each day, and a shared grocery table to send a day's or a week's ingredients straight to the list. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only view of the plan. Meals live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement until the owner moves them to shared tables, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Member Manager
items.description: View and manage a roster of people and their roles within an organization, including an optional phone number for each member. Member entries are stored in a shared SyncTable so every space member sees the same list. Email is a one-tap mailto link; a phone number offers a call/text chooser. Per-placement preferences (org name, available roles, edit policy) are stored in a local JSON file.

items.name: Member Reachout
items.description: Send updates and notifications to the people in your roster. Reads the same shared Members SyncTable as the Member Manager frame (bind it to the same table when prompted), so names, roles, emails and optional phone numbers stay in one place. Compose a message, pick who hears it (a role, several roles, or everyone), then send it as one bcc email or hand-text everyone with a phone number — one tap at a time. Every send is logged locally (date, audience, method) so you can browse the backlog and re-send later. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, see the message history for whichever roles you choose to expose.

items.name: Notes
items.description: Somewhere to put a thought before it goes. The box at the top is always open and always ready, so capturing something takes one keystroke and no decisions — no title, no folder, no file. Notes stack up newest first, grouped under the day they were written, and any word you start with a # becomes a tag you can filter by later. Space editors write and edit; everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, reads the same stream live. Deliberately not the Document frame: that one is for a page you sit down to write, this one is for the thing you would otherwise text yourself. Notes live in an encrypted LocalTable scoped to the placement.

items.name: Outpost
items.description: A lightweight public posting board for sharing with the world. Space members (editors) publish short posts — a passing thought, an open question, a status update, an announcement, a quick poll, or an image / audio / video clip — and anyone with the frame's share link can read them. Each post shows its author and the time it was shared, and URLs in the text become clickable (opened safely in the reader's browser). Posts live entirely in the frame's own data folder: one subfolder per placement holds a encrypted LocalTable (posts, media rows, and poll votes — indexed so a large, active feed stays fast) plus a per-post subfolder for any attached media bytes. Local file only, no sync tables.

items.name: Picture Frame
items.description: A digital picture frame for a space. Space editors drop photos in — by clicking Add or dragging them from the desktop — and everyone sees them as a grid of thumbnails; tap one and it fills the frame, tap again to go back. Turn on slideshow mode and the frame cycles through the photos at an interval you choose. There is one shared display: whatever an editor puts up is what every viewer sees, and the frame remembers exactly what it was showing, so a restarted frame or a rebooted machine comes back to the same photo. Viewer-role members and anonymous link visitors can browse the photos on their own screen without changing what the frame displays for anyone else. Photos are downscaled on the way in and stored with their bytes on the host beside a per-placement encrypted LocalTable; nothing leaves the device.

items.name: Recipe Box
items.description: The family recipe collection, unique per placement. Space editors store recipes with ingredients, steps, servings, tags, and notes, then read them from a clean cooking view set like a well-made recipe card. Search and tag filters keep a growing collection easy to browse. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only view of the collection. Recipes live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement, and the owner can graduate the collection to a shared table so the Meal Planner and future kitchen frames work over the same recipes. Every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Roadmap
items.description: A simple, robust project roadmapping tool — one roadmap per placement. Set a project name, overview, and quick links; break the work into milestones with target dates; and track dozens of small tasks per milestone through three states (unstarted, in-progress, complete), claiming and checking them off as you go. Drag tasks between milestones (or the Back Burner / Maybe Later buckets) to reprioritize, and within a milestone to rank them. Collapsed milestone headers still show live counts and a completed-per-day burn rate; a Timeline view lays out upcoming milestones with days-remaining and overdue color-coding. A milestone can only be marked done once all its tasks are complete. Everything is stored in a lightweight per-placement encrypted LocalTable database on the host and pushed live to every viewer; non-members get a read-only view.

items.name: Roundtable
items.description: A per-placement discussion + two prioritized idea boards for a space. Members chat in a single channel, add items to a Positives list (features/tasks) or a Negatives list (issues/bugs), and +1 the ones that matter. Items are ranked by votes, then recency. Only the owner can rename the frame and set high-level preferences. Non-members, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, follow along in a live read-only view.

items.name: RSS Reader
items.description: A reader for the open web, shared with the people you read alongside. Paste any site or feed address and the frame finds the feed, pulls the items in, and keeps them in groups you name. What you have read is yours alone; what you boost and what you say about an item is shared, so a space becomes a small room of co-readers rather than a lonely inbox. Keyboard-first: j and k move, m marks read, b boosts. Because a reader must be able to reach whatever you subscribe to, this frame asks for open network access — the platform answers by running it in a satellite process that can reach the wider internet but is blocked from your own machine and local network. Feeds, items and comments live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement.

items.name: Seamdeck
items.description: A tiny game console for your space. The frame is the whole device: a handheld on narrow screens, a TV + controller on wide ones. Members open sessions of little Phosphor-icon games (shot put, regatta, hot slice), join each other's lobbies, take turns or race in realtime, and chase the shared high-score board. Controls: D-pad via arrows/WASD, O = primary, I = secondary/back. It's also a template — each game is a self-contained two-file cartridge, and the console gives every cartridge lobbies, turn rotation, realtime racing, spectators, results, and high scores for free, so forking it into your own console is mostly writing games.

items.name: Slideshow
items.description: A simple presentation maker and presenter, unique per placement. Space editors build a deck of slides — stylized text (headings, body, bullet lists), uploaded images, and shapes — laid out freely on a fixed slide canvas; everything is positioned and sized proportionally so the deck looks identical from a 300×300 tile up to a scaled-up fullscreen presentation. Viewers can browse and present the deck but cannot edit it. The deck follows the space's channel color; a few show-wide settings (background, slide aspect, and an optional "keep viewers in sync" mode that locks every viewer's presentation to the editor's current slide) sit alongside the slides. The whole deck lives in a single JSON file in a per-placement folder, with uploaded images (auto-resized to keep file sizes reasonable) stored beside it. No database or sync tables.

items.name: Space Radio
items.description: A synced web radio player for everyone in a space. Space editors pick a station from a large list of public web stations — rock, pop, ambient, jazz, French, Italian, Australian, NPR, chiptune, and more — and everyone else, including anyone you share the frame with publicly, listens along to the same audio simultaneously. Play/pause and station selection are shared; each viewer's volume and mute are local and remembered between sessions.

items.name: Trip Planner
items.description: Plan a trip end to end, unique per placement. Space editors create trips and build each one out across three views: a day-by-day itinerary with times, activities, and places, a packing list grouped by category with live packed counts, and a running log of trip costs with a total. Places you name are looked up once and pinned on a map above the itinerary, so the whole trip reads at a glance. Everyone else, including anyone the frame is shared with publicly, sees a live read-only itinerary, so a share link doubles as the trip's printed handout. Trips live in encrypted LocalTables scoped to the placement, and every change is pushed live to all viewers.

items.name: Watercolor Studio
items.description: A quiet, beautiful place to paint with watercolors. Each placement is its own sheet of textured paper. Pigments are real watercolor pans — pick one, or add bits of several into the mixing well and they blend subtractively the way paint actually does (blue plus yellow makes green, complements make mud). A range of brushes (broad wash, round, flat, dry-brush, fine detail) lay translucent washes that pool, bleed, and darken at their edges; layered strokes glaze over one another. A clean-water Lift brush pulls pigment back out. Optional thin guide outlines (a pear, a teacup, a koi, a mountain lake…) sit faintly beneath the paint so new painters can trace as they learn. Editors in the space paint together in real time; anonymous viewers watch read-only. The whole painting is stored as deterministic vector strokes in a single JSON file per placement — no database, no network.

items.name: Weather Info
items.description: Example weather info/forecast using keyless API (open meteo)
